newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay net in line, cost control praised.
newsitem.headline: Cathay net in line, cost control praised.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd's 1996 net profit was in line with market expectations and analysts praised the Hong Kong flag carrier's ability to control costs and said profit growth should remain firm.

Cathay Pacific posted a rise of 27.9 percent in 1996 net profit on Wednesday to HK$3.81 billion, boosted by an exceptional gain of HK$541.0 million from the sale of most of Cathay's stake in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd.
Analysts estimates had ranged from HK$3.7 billion to HK$4.0 billion.

"They have done quite well. The results are broadly in line with our expectations," said Merrill Lynch analyst Wendy Wong. "On the cost side they have actually done better. They are obviously cutting costs quite aggressively."
Cathay Pacific said its total airline operating costs rose 6.5 percent to HK$26.67 billion, of which net finance charges represented HK$385 million down 35.8 percent on 1995.
It said increasing cost pressures and declining yields had required constant attention in 1996.

"The net (profit) was slightly better, particularly on the finance charge side," said Mark Simpson, director of Hong Kong research at ING Barings. "That was lower than I expected. That was really the swing factor."

Simpson, who had predicted 1996 net profit of HK$3.72 billion, said Cathay may have seen lower than expected capital expenditure in 1996 at Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport and spending could be more heavily weighted in 1997.
Cathay Pacific said it plans total capital expenditure of nearly HK$20 billion for the coming two to three years.

BZW Asia analyst K.Y. Ng said the results were "satisfactory". He said maintenance expenses, which rose significantly last year, should not be as high in 1997 and "the fuel price is expected to drop this year".

"This year's profit is expected to be good," Ng said. "In 1998 there will be a new airport in Hong Kong. It will benefit Hong Kong-based carriers, especially Cathay Pacific. The outlook is good for the local aviation market," he said.
Simpson forecast 1997 underlying earnings growth of 13 percent. "We are saying buy at current values," he said.
But he added that investors would have to keep an eye on yen movements. "The yen is still negative and I expect some strengthening to be seen in second half," Simpson said.
Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities, also saw a stronger yen helping 1997 earnings.
"A soft Japanese yen hurt its (1996) earnings but we expect an improvement in earnings in 1997 due to a stronger yen," he said.
Cathay Pacific shares rose HK$0.05 to close at HK$12.00 on Wednesday ahead of the results announcement.
